The $18,995 Ford Custom Garage Bronco ORV Package Ticks All the Right Off-Road Boxes
26 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford came up with a new way to sell Bronco customers the aftermarket through dealers. The ORV Package has just landed in the Ford Custom Garage catalog as a dealer-installed option, stacking a lot of stuff that makes a world of difference off the beaten path. Said package retails at $18,995 and is compatible with three models: four-door Base, Big Bend, and the Outer Banks.
From the standpoint of capability, the biggest upgrade over the four-door Base, Big Bend, and Outer Banks is FOX off-road suspension. Not only does it tighten damping and improve articulation, but additional ground clearance is a must for off-roading shenanigans. The package further transplants the Raptor's front and fuel tank plates, belly armor that said trims have never carried.
Rocker panel trail armor guards the sills on trails that tend to bite, whereas the modular front bumper pulls off the trick certain aftermarket bumpers do not manage. Specifically, the Ford -designed modular bumper keeps all sensors functional. RIGID auxiliary lighting tucks into that bumper. An auxiliary switch kit runs them, plus whatever powered gadget may come next.
The included ProCal tool is there for loading custom calibrations, with said tool doubling as a data logger. Matte-black WELD alloy wheels are in the offing as well, measuring 17 by 8.5 inches at every corner. These alloys ship with black lug nuts and no rubber, which means that customers have to source 315/70 R17 tires.
Otherwise put, the package will set you back more than $18,995. And that's before dealer pricing and installation charges. The rest of the package is all about identity, beginning with red tow hooks, Havoc fender flares, and red grille lettering. A stealth hood decal and a smoked Ford oval are featured as well.
Photo: Ford The visual treatment continues with a black tailgate badge and ORV fender badging. As implied, ORV stands for off-road vehicle. All components carry a supplemental three-year warranty honored at any Ford dealer nationwide. Bolting the kit does not void the factory coverage. Better still, any dealer or ASE-certified tech can do the install without touching the standard warranties.
As you may remember, Ford previewed this package as a concept at the 202 SEMA Show in Las Vegas. Less than a year to mature from a concept into a catalog item is pretty sweet, and that's not all. Optional extras include an ARB air compressor, a hydraulic hood lift kit, and a Borla high-clearance exhaust.
A heavy-duty rear diff cover is also available, as are Ford Performance sill plates and RIGID pods for the hood and roof. As of this writing, the ORV Package is described as a limited edition by its maker. Ford hasn't said how many will be produced for the US market.
It's not clear whether an ORV Package is coming for the 2027 model year Bronco as well. Instead of the familiar 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6, the 2027 levels up to the 3.0-liter EcoBoost V6 . In addition to the Bronco, the 2.7 is gone from the Ranger and F-150 as well.
